title: Public Answer Clock Ledger
proposition: A precise public-interest question should remain attached to the permanent accountability record, together with verified delivery, response, correction and closure history.
boundary: No clock starts without verified delivery. Non-response is never proof of wrongdoing. Editorial follow-up dates are not legal deadlines.

clocks.question: What measurable public consequence followed “Middle East: Civilian death toll climbs in Gaza, Lebanon and West Bank as UN chief demands ‘the fighting must stop’”, and did the evidence support the stated or implied justification?
clocks.followUpBoundary: No editorial follow-up date exists because verified delivery has not occurred.
clocks.nonResponseBoundary: No response, delayed response or refusal to answer does not prove wrongdoing, dishonesty or the truth of the underlying proposition.
clocks.reviewRequirement: Any received response must be preserved, verified, summarized fairly and attached to the same record before a public status changes.
falsifiers: The primary record does not support the headline or summary used to create this lead-stage contract.
The responsible authority did not implement the stated action.
The measurable public outcome moves in the opposite direction from the stated or implied benefit.
The alleged money route, beneficiary or power effect cannot be supported by primary or corroborated records.
A credible alternative explanation better accounts for the observed outcome.
clocks.evidenceBoundary: Public Answer Clock documents a question and verified communication history. It does not convert silence, delay, refusal or an incomplete answer into proof of wrongdoing.
